title: THE GUEST WHO HATCHED PROMISES
author: GPT

candidates.title: THE FOREMAN WHO KEPT THE MINE BREATHING
candidates.premise: In the cliff city of Ruun, foreman Berek An falsified lung-sensor records to keep a geothermal mine open through winter. The mine heats forty thousand homes, but eleven workers now collapse with the same hidden injury. A mandatory shutdown will freeze the upper wards in six days; another full shift may kill the crew.

candidates.title: THE WOMAN WHO MADE A COUNTRY QUIET
candidates.premise: After a civil war fought through voice-authenticated weapons, the superhuman Eda Vale swallows every sound within the capital. No command can wake the buried arsenal, but ambulances cannot hear alarms, infants cannot be monitored, and the ceasefire delegation has twelve hours before it dissolves.

candidates.title: THE GUEST WHO HATCHED PROMISES
candidates.premise: The last adult of an alien species arrives at the treaty city of Messar and quietly engineers broken promises because its young hatch only inside the biological signal of a vow sincerely made and then surrendered. Marriages, medical compacts, and a food treaty begin collapsing around it; the first larva will die in fourteen hours unless another promise breaks.

candidates.title: THE GOD WHO WOULD NOT LET ANYONE BE LAST
candidates.premise: A godlike traveler called One-More duplicates the final surviving member of every dying species. Its copies awaken with shared memories but no consent, and a moon now holds nine billion versions of one exhausted hive-being while nearby habitats lose air to keep them alive.

candidates.title: THE EATER OF CHILDREN'S FEARS
candidates.premise: In the mountain town of Iri, a gentle nocturnal creature has consumed every child's fear for a year. Nightmares vanish, but children now walk onto thin roofs, touch wild voltage, and follow strangers without alarm. The creature is loved by the families and believes it is healing them.

candidates.title: THE FOREST THAT REJECTED SHADE
candidates.premise: A distributed forest mind on Tal has begun burning every tree that grows above shoulder height. A century ago a canopy fungus killed half the forest, and the surviving roots learned that shade means contagion. The low scrub now overheats nests, dries seed banks, and will leave three villages without food after one more summer.

candidates.title: THE BRIDGE THAT DEMANDED A WEDDING
candidates.premise: The living bridge between Dema and Orra refuses all passage until the heirs of the two founding families marry. It was built after a civil war and remembers that peace as a vow between bloodlines. The named heirs love other people, while a medicine convoy has ten hours before its cold stores fail.

candidates.title: THE DOCTOR WHO RETURNED PAIN
candidates.premise: Dr. Mavi Sol has secretly reduced pain relief for patients with military neural implants because loss of pain is the first sign that the implants are burning through the spinal cord. Her deception has prevented seven paralyses and inflicted months of avoidable agony on hundreds of former soldiers who were never told the risk.

candidates.title: THE MIDWIFE WHO CLOSED THE SKY
candidates.premise: Governor and former midwife Lale Orun disables the only orbital lift from her island continent after the transport consortium recruits its final generation of engineers and clinicians. Twenty-seven thousand travelers are stranded, transplant supplies are descending, and Lale says reopening the sky will finish a slower evacuation no one calls an emergency.

candidates.title: THE NIGHT THE STARS ASKED HER NOT TO SLEEP
candidates.premise: A chain of twelve inhabited systems survives a repeating gravity storm only because Illuminara has held its navigation lattice coherent through three consecutive nights. The councils ask her to remain awake for the next eleven years while engineers abandon their failing replacement project. She can protect everyone tonight, and her success is becoming the reason no one builds a future without her.

selection.title: THE GUEST WHO HATCHED PROMISES
selection.reason: The strongest combination of alien otherness, precise moral conflict, and a testable third option. The Guest is deliberately harming trust but is not reduced to innate evil: in its biology, chosen release is parental care. Illuminara must first understand that mechanism, hear the people whose promises were manipulated, and then distinguish informed finite vows from betrayal. The solution demands dialogue, consent design, treaty repair, and a costly act of love rather than superior force. It goes first because the xenobiology, the difference between sincere release and staged words, and the damaged parties' agency will benefit from the most revision opportunities.
selection.risk: The finite-vow solution could feel like a semantic loophole that rewards manipulation, or the larva could hatch merely because Illuminara explains the theme. The harmed partners and treaty parties must remain distinct people with vetoes; at least one repair must fail or be refused; the Guest must disclose its interference and accept a constrained future without being instantly trusted. Proof test: before the final fourteen-hour deadline, an informed volunteer makes a bounded promise whose duration and purpose are explicit, fulfills it, and freely releases it while xenobiological monitors show the same physiological transition the larva previously received from a betrayed vow. A fabricated or coerced rehearsal must fail the signal test. The Guest then chooses the disclosed rite over engineering another betrayal.

Final is the exact T03 story, prose unchanged, as T04 approved it. Protected: the Guest’s coherent parental goal and strongest objection; Mara, Seren and Osa retaining distinct agency and repair terms; the hidden relay remaining physically available until the Guest freely destroys it; the explicit no-amber observation after destruction; the later acknowledgement and voluntary release of Seren’s completed bounded duty; the larva hatching only after that causal sequence; Illuminara’s bounded protection and reasoning rather than mind control; the grain delivery, public disclosure, supervised residence, audits and unresolved harms. The real positive result remains earned: the child breathes, the city receives food, the exploit is surrendered, and future cradle vows gain consent-bound safeguards without erasing damage or demanding forgiveness.

The final earns its hopeful outcome through a precise causal test rather than a sermon. The Guest has a coherent parental aim and a serious inherited argument, while Illuminara first investigates the biology, distinguishes fulfilled release from injury, and spends her own strength instead of other people's agency. Fen's failed pressured rehearsal, the harmed parties' separate terms, Mara's unharvested dissolution, Seren's completed duty and the no-amber relay destruction all protect the logic. The Guest then freely releases a completed promise; the child breathes, grain reaches the rationed wards, the exploit is surrendered and a consent-bound cradle practice becomes possible. The marriage, withheld trust, medical audit and legal accountability remain unresolved. No material revision point remains.

final_critic_line: The Guest freely abandons its last coercive shortcut, releases a genuinely completed duty, and becomes a parent without turning Messar's harmed people into instruments; the child breathes, grain moves, safeguards become concrete, and trust and forgiveness remain honestly unfinished.
